_readme: One entry per blockchain. status: "live" = page built, listed and in the sitemap; "hidden" = nothing is built or linked. After editing, run: node site-src/build.mjs. Required: slug, name, ticker, color, features, status. Optional: icon (file name in site-icons/ without .svg; defaults to the lower-case ticker), glyph and fg (no longer drawn; kept as fallback data), kind (evm | utxo | solana | tron | cardano | account), tokens, notes (short, factual sentences shown on the chain page), staking (how staking works there).

chains.name: Bitcoin
notes: Native SegWit (bc1q…) and Taproot (bc1p…) addresses.
Transactions are checked before you sign: unknown scripts, OP_RETURN data or a fee above 100 sat/vB ask for a second confirmation.
Bitcoin has no native staking.

chains.name: Ethereum
notes: ETH and ERC-20 tokens in the same account.
Token approvals are set to the exact amount by default. Unlimited approvals are off unless you turn them on.
Contract calls, approvals and high fees ask for a second confirmation.
Native ETH staking is not offered: it needs 32 ETH and a validator running at all times. Liquid staking with Lido and lending on Aave are in Earn.

chains.name: BNB Chain
notes: Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in BNB.

chains.name: Polygon
notes: Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in POL.

chains.name: Arbitrum
notes: Arbitrum One, an Ethereum layer 2.
Same address as your Ethereum account. Network fees are paid in ETH.

chains.name: Optimism
notes: OP Mainnet, an Ethereum layer 2.
Same address as your Ethereum account. Network fees are paid in ETH.

chains.name: Base
notes: An Ethereum layer 2.
Same address as your Ethereum account. Network fees are paid in ETH.

chains.name: Avalanche
notes: Kyro uses the Avalanche C-Chain.
Same address as your Ethereum account. Network fees are paid in AVAX.

chains.name: Cronos
notes: Cronos EVM. Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in CRO.

chains.name: Mantle
notes: Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in MNT.

chains.name: Sonic
notes: Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in S.

chains.name: Flare
notes: Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in FLR.

chains.name: Kaia
notes: Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in KAIA.

chains.name: Gnosis
notes: Gnosis Chain. Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in xDAI.

chains.name: HyperEVM
notes: The EVM side of Hyperliquid. Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in HYPE.

chains.name: Sei
notes: Sei EVM. Same address as your Ethereum account.
Network fees are paid in SEI.

chains.name: Conflux
notes: Kyro uses Conflux eSpace, the EVM-compatible side of Conflux.
Same address as your Ethereum account. Network fees are paid in CFX.

chains.name: Solana
chains.staking: Delegate SOL to a validator from a stake account in your name. Activation and cooldown take about one epoch each (around two days). A validator cannot take your SOL; your rewards depend on its commission and uptime.
notes: SOL, SPL and Token-2022 tokens.
Versioned (v0) transactions and address lookup tables are decoded before you sign.

chains.name: TRON
chains.staking: Stake TRX (Stake 2.0) for energy or bandwidth, then vote for Super Representatives with your TRON Power. Unstaking takes 14 days. Votes do not put your TRX at risk.
notes: TRX and TRC-20 tokens such as USDT.
Energy and bandwidth from staking lower the cost of TRC-20 transfers.

chains.name: Cardano
chains.staking: Delegate to a stake pool. Your ADA stays on your address and remains spendable. Registering costs a 2 ADA deposit, returned when you stop.
notes: ADA and Cardano native tokens.
Standard Shelley addresses (addr1…).
chains.hwNote: Not on the Trezor One. A Ledger gives different Cardano addresses than the software wallet for the same phrase.

chains.name: XRP Ledger
notes: XRP and issued currencies.
Destination tags for exchanges and custodial services.
Every XRP Ledger account keeps a small reserve that cannot be sent.
The XRP Ledger has no native staking.

chains.name: Litecoin
notes: Native SegWit (ltc1…) addresses.
Litecoin has no native staking.

chains.name: Dogecoin
notes: Standard Dogecoin addresses (D…).
Input amounts are read from the previous transactions and checked before you sign.
Dogecoin has no native staking.

chains.name: Bitcoin Cash
notes: Bitcoin Cash has no native staking.

chains.name: Dash
notes: Standard Dash addresses (X…).

chains.name: Stellar
notes: Stellar accounts need a minimum balance of XLM to exist on the network.
USDC on Stellar is supported. The account needs a USDC trustline to hold it.
Stellar has no native staking.
chains.swapNote: Swap into XLM from other chains (Stellar is a destination only for now).

chains.name: NEAR
notes: NEAR Protocol mainnet.
USDC and USDT on NEAR are supported.
chains.hwNote: The Ledger account is a different account than the software wallet.
chains.swapNote: Swap native NEAR in and out through Exolix, without an account. Kyro's fee is a second ordinary transfer on NEAR. NEAR tokens are not offered.
chains.staking: Stake with a NEAR staking pool from the official factories. Kyro checks the pool's code before each transaction. Unstaked NEAR stays locked for 4 epochs before you can withdraw it. With a Ledger account, staking is not available.

chains.name: Sui
notes: Sui mainnet. Network fees are paid in SUI.
USDC on Sui is supported.

chains.name: Monero
notes: Your Kyro recovery phrase restores your Monero wallet too. To move it to another Monero wallet, Kyro can also show the matching 25-word Monero phrase, which works in Monero GUI, Feather and Cake.
Balance and history are scanned on your computer, so your view key never leaves it. Kyro scans against a regular monerod node, over Tor.
The first sync of an old restored wallet can take a while.
Monero has no native staking.
chains.swapNote: Swap XMR both ways through Exolix, without an account. Kyro's fee is a second ordinary transfer of the coin you sell.

chains.name: TON
notes: TON is the network. Its coin is Gram (GRAM), renamed from Toncoin in June 2026.
USDT on TON is supported.
v4R2 wallet. The same recovery phrase gives the same address as Trust Wallet. Tonkeeper uses its own phrase format, so its addresses will not match.
The wallet contract is deployed on your first send.
chains.hwNote: The Ledger wallet has a different address than the software wallet. Comments: printable ASCII, up to 120 characters.

chains.name: Cosmos Hub
notes: Cosmos Hub addresses (cosmos1…).
Transfers are simulated before you sign.
Staking is not available yet.

chains.name: Polkadot
notes: Balance and transfers are on Asset Hub.
The system confirmation window shows the existential deposit, the minimum balance an account must keep.

chains.name: Aptos
notes: Aptos mainnet. Network fees are paid in APT.
USDC and USDT on Aptos are supported.

chains.name: Algorand
notes: The minimum balance of the account is shown before you send.
Same address as the Ledger Algorand app for the same recovery phrase.
chains.swapNote: Swap native ALGO in and out through Exolix, without an account. Kyro's fee is a second ordinary transfer on Algorand. Algorand tokens are not offered.

chains.name: Kaspa
notes: Standard Kaspa addresses (kaspa:…).
Kaspa has no native staking.
chains.swapNote: Swap native KAS in and out through Exolix, without an account. Kyro's fee is a second ordinary transfer on Kaspa.

chains.name: Hedera
notes: Receive on the EVM-style address (0x…). The 0.0.x account is created when the first deposit arrives.
chains.hwNote: The account must be created with Ledger Live or HashPack first; it is a different account than the software wallet.

chains.name: Zcash
notes: Transparent addresses (t…) only. Shielded addresses are not supported.
Zcash has no native staking.
